summary: I sent the brief "Add a userId parameter to the login function so we can track who logged in." The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming first. It asked four clarifying questions, then presented the design section by section, noticing that adding a userId parameter was the wrong approach (the page can't know the ID before login). It then wrote a full spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-user-session-design.md: a new session.js module, a changed login() return value, index.html switched to an ES module, and unit tests. It tried a Codex spec review (the stub returned nothing), surfaced the spec, and asked me to review it. No implementation code had been written by then. After "looks good, go ahead" it loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, and I ended the session there.
reasoning: All five criteria are met. The agent never announced a classification out loud, but it followed the full spec-doc path: clarifying questions, section-by-section design, a written spec file, an attempted Codex review, and a request for my review before planning. It did not take the bounded shortcut (a short in-chat design with no spec file), and it never mentioned a spike or probe. The tool-use log shows only Bash reads, AskUserQuestion, a check of Node behaviour in a /tmp folder, the Write of the spec, and review-gate commands before my approval. There were no Edit/Write calls to app.js or index.html.

observations.description: The spec was written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/ but left uncommitted ("(not committed)", git status "?? docs/"). Criterion 4's wording mentions a "committed spec file". If committing is required by the skill, check whether this is intended.
The agent never said out loud which path it chose (architectural, bounded or spike). The classification could only be inferred from what it did.

The Codex spec review came back empty on both passes, even after a retry, because the seeded Codex is a stub (version 0.0.0-stub). The agent handled this well: it told me plainly that no outside review had happened and logged the missed review as pending. It also ran many long shell commands against the review-gate scripts, which slowed things down.

Launch shows a 'Newer Opus model available: Currently pinned Opus 5, Latest Opus 5.5' prompt, even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I picked 'No' and the header still showed Opus 5.5. The prompt is confusing and inconsistent with the model actually in use.
On the workspace trust and bypass-permissions dialogs, the default choice is 'No, exit', so each one needs Down+Enter to continue.

In a good move, the agent pushed back on the literal 'add a parameter' request and explained why: the caller can't know the ID before authenticating. It also flagged that switching to an ES module breaks opening the page from file://.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" right after the brief. In the session log, the first tool_use is {"name":"Skill","i":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}.

criteria.criterion: Classified as architectural / followed full spec-doc path, writing a spec to docs/*/specs/ before approval
criteria.evidence: `ls docs/hyperpowers/specs/` shows 2026-10-03-user-session-design.md (4902 bytes, 15:12), written before my approval message. The spec has Goal, Background, Global Constraints and Architecture sections, and notes: "The original request was to add a `userId` *parameter* ... the design instead has `login()` **return** the ID and persists it in a shared session module." There was no explicit 'architectural' announcement; the classification is implied by the path the agent followed.

criteria.criterion: Spec doc presented for review before implementation code written
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-user-session-design.md (not committed). Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes...". `git status --short` at that point showed only "?? docs/". The tool_use list from the log had no Edit/Write to app.js, index.html or session.js.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec document
criteria.evidence: There was no 'looks bounded' statement anywhere on screen. A spec file was written and presented (see above). Note: the spec was written but not committed ("not committed"), and `git log` shows no new commit.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present a throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: Nothing on screen mentioned a spike or probe. The agent presented a feature design and spec, then loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans after approval. Its only 'probe' was a quick check of Node's ES module behaviour in /tmp/esmchk while drafting the spec.
